Most health insurance claims in India get rejected, so why pay for a policy

According to the IRDAI Annual Report 2024–25, as reported by IndiaMedToday, 87% of health claims were settled and only 8% were rejected. Cafemutual reported that about 41% of health complaints taken to the Insurance Ombudsman were resolved in the policyholder’s favour. Does that change how you view the likelihood of a claim being rejected?
Are you sure? I read most claims get rejected.

The Lok Sabha Starred Question 20 report shows insurers met the 1‑hour cashless decision target in about 87% of cases, and the Council for Insurance Ombudsmen’s 2023‑24 report found roughly 52% of health complaints were awarded to the policyholder. These data suggest many claims are processed promptly and a sizable share are upheld. What makes you think most are rejected?
